title: The quiet advantage of a personal operating system
author: Pratik Bajoria
excerpt: The best productivity stack is not the one with the most tools. It is the one that turns good intentions into repeatable decisions.
content: A useful personal operating system is a small set of decisions you make consistently: what you measure, what you ignore, and where automation earns its place. This note is a starting point for building one without confusing activity for leverage.

title: A decision framework for buying your first investment property
author: Pratik Bajoria
excerpt: A practical way to think about yield, leverage, vacancy, and the opportunity cost of your next rupee.
content: Property is a long-duration decision with a short list of variables that matter: cash flow, financing terms, location quality, liquidity, and downside resilience. Model the base case before falling in love with the asset.

title: Compounding is a behaviour before it is a number
author: Pratik Bajoria
excerpt: Why the most valuable financial habit is building a process that survives both optimism and fear.
content: Compounding needs a process that can operate when markets are boring and when they are loud. The practical work is setting an allocation policy, defining risk in advance, and reviewing it on a calendar rather than in reaction to headlines.
